reproduction_target: The ChIP-seq sequence-analysis pipeline described in Methods > 'Sequencing data analysis', applied to the authors' own deposited data (GEO GSE304259, BioProject PRJNA1299792): bcl2fastq demultiplexing -> Trimmomatic adapter trimming -> FastQC -> Bowtie 2 alignment to hg38 (default parameters) -> SAMtools markdup duplicate removal -> HOMER makeTagDirectory (MAPQ > 10) / makeBigWig.pl / findPeaks (-style histone; -style histone -size 1000 -minDist 2500; -style factor, matched input as background) / mergePeaks / annotatePeaks.pl (hg38, -size 2000; TSS and peak histograms hg38, -size 4000, -hist 10) -> deepTools computeMatrix + plotHeatmap -> custom Python (matplotlib/seaborn) scatterplots and coverage histograms. External reference peak set: ENCODE CTCF file accession ENCFF502CZS (Fig. 3D,E). The entire wet-lab arm (spa-ChIP-seq protocol development on the Agilent Bravo liquid handler, cross-linking/shearing/IP/library-prep/sequencing) is out of the computational reproduction target and is counted as W.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation, derived entirely from Methods prose (no workflow file, no repository, no code read). The paper is a wet-lab automation/protocol paper whose computational arm is a conventional ChIP-seq analysis using standard public tools; |S| = 14 computational steps, |W| = 8 wet-lab steps (cell culture and cross-linking; chromatin shearing; sheared-chromatin analysis and input prep; ChIP; ChIP washes; library construction and reverse cross-linking; PCR amplification and final cleanup; DNA quantification and Illumina NextSeq sequencing). SOURCE SUBSTITUTION: the bioRxiv JATS XML for this preprint could not be retrieved (WebFetch 403; curl 429 / Cloudflare 'error code: 1015' rate limit on two attempts). Methods, Data access, and abstract were read instead from the peer-reviewed version of the SAME paper (Genome Res 2026;36(1):129-141, doi 10.1101/gr.281320.125, PMC12758389) via NCBI efetch, whose title matched the v3 preprint title verbatim; GEO sample-level data_processing fields were also inspected and add no version information. If the v3 preprint carries a Code availability statement absent from the journal version, this report under-reports it. Stage-1 prose only: no workflow source read, env_capture_class 'n/a' throughout, R-star not assignable.

steps.label: Demultiplexing of raw sequencing output with Illumina bcl2fastq ('Raw sequencing data were demultiplexed using Illumina's bcl2fastq program')
Adapter trimming with Trimmomatic ('Adapter sequences were trimmed with Trimmomatic (Bolger et al. 2014)')
Read-quality assessment with FastQC ('sequencing quality was assessed using FastQC')
Alignment to the human reference genome (hg38) with Bowtie 2 using the default parameters
Duplicate-read removal with SAMtools markdup ('duplicated reads were removed with SAMtools markdup')
HOMER makeTagDirectory to build tag directories of filtered primary alignments (MAPQ > 10)
bigWig track generation with HOMER makeBigWig.pl for IGV visualization
Peak calling with HOMER findPeaks ('-style histone'; '-style histone -size 1000 -minDist 2500'; '-style factor' for TFs) using matched input controls as background
Retrieval of external CTCF peak set from the ENCODE Project Consortium, file accession ENCFF502CZS (used in Fig. 3D,E)
Merging of peaks across all samples per antibody target with HOMER mergePeaks
Read-depth-normalized read-count quantification at merged peak regions with HOMER annotatePeaks.pl (hg38, -size 2000)
TSS-centered and peak-centered histograms with HOMER annotatePeaks.pl in 'TSS' mode or with peak files (hg38, -size 4000, -hist 10)
Heatmaps centered on TSSs and peaks generated with deepTools computeMatrix and plotHeatmap
All other plots (scatterplots, coverage histograms) generated with custom Python scripts using matplotlib and seaborn (see Supplemental Code)
Cell culture and fixation (cross-linking): single (FA) or double (DSG+FA) cross-linking of HeLa-S3 / HEK293T-BRD4-FKBP12F36V-2xHA cells
Chromatin shearing (96-well sonication; lysis buffer comparison LB3 vs EBB)
Analysis of sheared chromatin / input preparation (manual and Bravo workflows)
Chromatin immunoprecipitation (manual and Agilent Bravo automated workflows)
ChIP washes (manual and Bravo workflows)
Library construction, reverse cross-linking, and library cleanup (NEBNext Ultra II, NEXTflex barcodes, Speedbeads)
PCR amplification and final cleanup of ChIP and input libraries
DNA quantification (agarose gel, Qubit HS DNA) and sequencing on Illumina NextSeq 500 or NextSeq 2000

headline.static_readiness: 0/14 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 1/14 (7%) readiness upper bound at Stage 1. Only C9 (retrieval of ENCODE file accession ENCFF502CZS) reaches RI, because an immutable ENCODE file accession is itself an exact pin. The other 13 computational steps drop to NI on the Version axis: the paper states NO version number for ANY piece of software - bcl2fastq, Trimmomatic, FastQC, Bowtie 2, SAMtools, HOMER, deepTools, IGV, Python, matplotlib, seaborn are all named without versions, and the GEO sample-level data_processing fields repeat the same prose with no versions either. C1 (bcl2fastq demultiplexing) additionally fails the Data axis because the BCL inputs are not deposited (GEO provides processed FASTQ/bigWig), and bcl2fastq is license-gated Illumina software. capture_claim is 'none': no lockfile, no container, no conda environment, no requirements file, not even scattered version tokens, so this paper is NOT a stage2 R-star candidate - even a perfect Stage-2 code check could not lift Version above 0/1. Symmetric qualifier (guide R-star section): this 0 under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency, and the analysis uses only widely available standard tools, so the practical barrier is version drift rather than inaccessibility.
headline.coverage: 14 computational steps assessed from Methods prose ('Sequencing data analysis' paragraph, the paper's only computational Methods section). 8 wet-lab steps (W=8) constitute the paper's primary contribution (the automated spa-ChIP-seq bench protocol) and are OOS. Computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 14/22 = 64%. Data are the authors' own, publicly deposited (GEO GSE304259, public since 2025-10-30). NO code repository (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage) is stated anywhere in the paper; the 'software files' offered under Data access are Agilent Bravo / VWorks instrument protocol files for the wet-lab automation, and the only analysis code referenced is 'Supplemental Code' for the plotting scripts.

gaps.where: Methods > Sequencing data analysis; also GEO GSE304259 sample-level !Sample_data_processing fields
gaps.missing: Gap 2a (version not recorded) applies to every single tool in the computational arm: bcl2fastq, Trimmomatic, FastQC, Bowtie 2, SAMtools (markdup), HOMER (makeTagDirectory, makeBigWig.pl, findPeaks, mergePeaks, annotatePeaks.pl), deepTools (computeMatrix, plotHeatmap), IGV, Python, matplotlib, seaborn. No requirements file, no conda environment, no lockfile, no container. HOMER in particular is version- and config-sensitive (the hg38 genome/annotation package installed into HOMER is not identified).
gaps.how_to_close: State exact versions for every tool in the Methods, and ship a conda-lock / pixi.lock / renv.lock or a container image referenced by digest that pins interpreter, channels and platform.

gaps.missing: No public code repository is stated. The Data access statement deposits data (GEO GSE304259) and wet-lab automation artifacts ('deck layouts, detailed parameters, and software files (Supplemental Files)' = Agilent Bravo/VWorks instrument protocols) but deposits no analysis pipeline. Consequently the exact command lines are unrecoverable for: Trimmomatic (adapter FASTA, ILLUMINACLIP/SLIDINGWINDOW/MINLEN settings), SAMtools markdup (whether -r was used, and the sort/fixmate preamble), makeBigWig.pl (normalization, resolution, -strand), mergePeaks (-d and which samples were pooled per target), and deepTools computeMatrix/plotHeatmap (reference-point vs scale-regions, window, bin size, sorting, normalization, colormap).
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the driver scripts for the full alignment/peak-calling/quantification/figure pipeline in a public versioned repository (GitHub + Zenodo DOI or Software Heritage), and reference it from a Code availability statement.

gaps.where: Methods > Sequencing data analysis (Bowtie 2 alignment step C4; HOMER annotatePeaks.pl steps C11-C12)
gaps.missing: The reference genome is named only as 'the human reference genome (hg38)'. No source (UCSC / GENCODE / NCBI analysis set), no patch level, no accession, no URL, no checksum, no statement of whether decoys/alts/chrEBV were included, and no description of how the Bowtie 2 index was built. Likewise the HOMER 'hg38' genome/annotation package version used by annotatePeaks.pl (which determines the TSS set) is unspecified. This is out-of-band, unpinned reference-resource distribution; because Stage 1 does not read code, no A/B/C env_capture_class is assigned.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact reference FASTA (provider + release/patch + accession or checksum), the exact Bowtie 2 index build command, and the HOMER genome package version.

gaps.where: Methods > Sequencing data analysis (step C1, demultiplexing)
gaps.missing: bcl2fastq is proprietary, license-gated Illumina software (registration required, now deprecated in favour of BCL Convert), and the BCL run folders it consumes are not deposited - GEO GSE304259 supplies processed FASTQ/bigWig only. The demultiplexing step therefore cannot be re-run from public inputs. Impact is limited: the step is skippable because its outputs (per-sample FASTQ) are the deposited artifacts.
gaps.how_to_close: State the bcl2fastq version and deposit the sample sheets, or explicitly declare demultiplexing as out of the reproduction path since FASTQ are deposited.

gaps.where: Methods > Sequencing data analysis, final sentence (step C14)
gaps.missing: 'All other plots (e.g., scatterplots and coverage histograms) were generated with custom Python scripts using matplotlib and seaborn (see Supplemental Code).' The scripts exist only as journal supplemental material - not a versioned, independently citable, dependency-declaring artifact. Whether the supplement is runnable (entry point, input schema, dependency list) is unverifiable at Stage 1 (subflag needs-supplement). Note that the canonical record here is the bioRxiv preprint, whose supplemental packaging may differ from the journal version's Supplemental Code.
gaps.how_to_close: Mirror the plotting scripts to Zenodo/GitHub with a DOI, an environment file, and a README stating which figure each script produces.

gaps.where: Methods > Cell culture and fixation ... through DNA quantification and sequencing (W1-W8)
gaps.missing: 8 wet-lab steps constitute the paper's primary contribution (the automated spa-ChIP-seq bench protocol on an Agilent Bravo). These are non-computational and OOS by NASEM 2019 scope; they are excluded from |S| and are not a defect. Computational coverage is therefore 14/22 = 64%.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - out of scope for Tier-1 computational reproducibility. The wet-lab arm is unusually well documented (deck layouts, VWorks protocol files, per-step parameters in Supplemental Files).
